title: Should Investors Buy Broadcom Stock Instead of Marvell Stock? | AVGO Stock vs. MRVL Stock
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; captions readable
summary: Parkevtate compares Broadcom and Marvell head-to-head across sales, profitability, ROIC and valuation to decide the better AI-semiconductor buy. Broadcom: sales boomed from ~$35B in early 2024 to ~$90B TTM (VMware acquisition integrating well); operating margin 48.6% (up from ~5% in 2017); ROIC 25.75%, more than 2x WACC. Marvell: operating margin 16.8% (about a third of Broadcom's); ROIC 12.61%, roughly at WACC; Jensen Huang suggested Marvell could become a trillion-dollar semiconductor company. Valuation: Marvell trades at 39x forward PE vs Broadcom's 18x — he questions whether Marvell deserves a more-than-2x premium. His DCF: Broadcom fair value $523 vs $353 market price (~48% upside over 12-18 months); Marvell fair value $207 vs $266 (~22% downside). Conclusion: Broadcom offers better business prospects; Marvell offers better forward upside in theory, but not at this valuation. He prefers Broadcom — owns it, doesn't own Marvell, isn't interested in Marvell near these levels, and prefers several other semis over Marvell. AI demand visibility runs through early 2028; beyond that are question marks. He also flags Micron's September 30 earnings as the next read on AI demand. Calls: AVGO BUY at $353 (DCF fair $523); MRVL AVOID at $266 (DCF fair $207). No stance flips — no prior parkevtate calls on AVGO/MRVL.
